nodes.title: One rank function for commands

anchor.snippet: function rank(title: string, query: string): number {

nodes.why: A prefix, a word start and a substring are three strengths of the same match. Returning a number per command makes the order one sort, with the list order as the tie-break.
nodes.alternative: Run three filters and concatenate them.
nodes.tradeoff: Three passes work too, but a command can land in two groups unless every filter excludes the ones before it.

nodes.title: next <weekday> skips today
nodes.why: The modulo gives 0 when the weekday is today; `|| 7` turns that into a week ahead, which is what someone typing `next thursday` on a Thursday means.
nodes.alternative: Treat `next <weekday>` as the weekday in the following calendar week.
nodes.tradeoff: That is another valid reading, but it must be stated; this task names the first such day after today.

nodes.title: Debounce inside the effect
nodes.why: The effect runs on every change of the query, and its cleanup clears the previous timer, so a search starts only once typing has paused for `DEBOUNCE_MS`.
nodes.alternative: Wrap the change handler in a debounced function.
nodes.tradeoff: A debounced callback needs a stable reference across renders and its own cleanup on unmount, which the effect gives for free.

nodes.title: Abort the request a newer query replaces
nodes.why: The answer to `pl` takes 500 ms and the one to `pla` 120 ms. Aborting in the cleanup means the slower, older answer is never set, whatever order they arrive in.
nodes.alternative: Keep a request counter and drop answers whose number is not the latest.
nodes.tradeoff: A counter works and suits APIs that cannot be cancelled, but the request still runs to the end.

nodes.title: An abort is not a failure
nodes.why: A cancelled request rejects too. Without this line every keystroke would flash the error state.
nodes.tradeoff: Equivalent here; the name check also covers an API that rejects for its own reasons with an AbortError.

nodes.title: Focus stays in the input
nodes.why: Typing must keep working while the arrows move through the options, so focus stays in the input and `aria-activedescendant` tells assistive technology which option is active.
nodes.alternative: Move real focus to each option.
nodes.tradeoff: Moving focus takes the caret out of the input, so the next keystroke would not type.
